name: conexus-tool-spill
description: Keeps big tool output out of your context with no setup. In the main conversation, a Bash output or whole-file Read over 4000 bytes is cut to its first 1400 and last 800 bytes, with a note saying where the full text is (Bash output is saved to a file), so one big command costs a few KB of context instead of all of it. Every option can stay blank: blank means the default shown in its name.

limit.title: Cut output larger than this many bytes (blank = 4000)
limit.description: The size at which a main-session Bash output or whole-file Read is cut. Raise it to see more output whole; lower it to save more context. Blank uses 4000.

head.title: Bytes kept from the start of a cut output (blank = 1400)
head.description: How much of the beginning the model still sees, cut back to a line end. Blank uses 1400.

tail.title: Bytes kept from the end, where errors and verdicts land (blank = 800)
tail.description: How much of the end of a cut Bash output the model still sees; a test run's summary or a script's failure is usually there. Blank uses 800.

includeHeadless.title: Also cut claude -p runs (default off)
includeHeadless.description: Off: headless runs (nx_answer operators, scripted critics) get full output, since nobody is there to follow the note. Turn on only to save context in those runs too.
